::: {#exr-calf-mute-canoe}
A monthly-payment function uses only principal, interest rate, and loan duration. Which is the best reason to treat its output as a model rather than a complete description of a real mortgage payment?

```{mcq}
#| label: d06-model-05
1. The function has inputs and therefore cannot be mathematical.
2. Real mortgages may also involve fees, insurance, or other dimensions not included in the function. [correct]
3. A model can never produce a numerical output.
4. The output must always be unrelated to the inputs.
```
:::
